item.text: The implementation matches the oracle across the validation set, including the empty-string and embedded-space cases that affect raw byte layout. I’m checking line numbers now so the close-out can point you straight to the entrypoint and the reusable modules.

Created the Rust Cargo project in [Cargo.toml](/output/Cargo.toml:1), with the requested entry file at [test11.rs](/output/test11.rs:1) and reusable logic split across [transform.rs](/output/src/idna/transform.rs:1) and [classify.rs](/output/src/idna/classify.rs:1). The implementation matches the oracle’s observed behavior, not real IDNA: `to_ascii` prefixes `xn--` after ASCII-only lowercasing, `to_unicode` strips one exact lowercase leading `xn--`, validity is just non-empty, ASCII/IDN classification is `is_ascii()`, and label count is `'.'` count plus 1.

I built `/output/test11` with `rustc --edition 2021 test11.rs -o test11` and `/output/target/release/test11` with `cargo build --release`. Both were byte-compared against `/workspace/dataset/test11_executable` and matched on the default run plus cases including `""`, `" "`, `"Example.COM"`, `"xn--Example.COM"`, `"日本語.jp"`, `"CAFÉ.COM"`, and mixed multi-argument invocations.
